look_here_first: Platte River milkvetch bears relatively large FLESHY pods that can resemble Berlandier's groundplum. Examine the developing OVARY and pod for fine HAIRS (usually pubescent in plattensis) and two GROOVED pod seams (sutures); the plump fruit alone is not distinctive.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Fabaceae/Astragalus: alternate pinnate leaves, papilionoid pea flowers, and legumes; fruit shape, inflation, hairiness, and curvature are especially useful for species ID.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial, sometimes sprawling from buried root/caudex branches

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rather broad pinnate leaves; flowers pea-shaped, often pink to purple-tinged

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: thick fleshy, somewhat rounded/ovoid pod around 1–1.7 cm long

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ovary and pod surface consistently hairy (pubescent), unlike normally glabrous groundplum

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature fruit grooved along dorsal and ventral sutures and often becomes firm/leathery

lookalikes.differences: Groundplum A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri and A. plattensis can look nearly identical in southcentral Texas. First check developing ovary/pod for hairs; then use mature grooves running along BOTH sutures. The installed pod photo shows fine hairs but no calibrated microscopic measure.
